title: HYPOTHESIS TESTING FOR QUANTIFYING LLM-HUMAN MISALIGNMENT IN MULTIPLE CHOICE SETTINGS

bias_targets.methodology: Hypothesis testing (permutation tests and Kolmogorov-Smirnov) comparing LLM-simulated response distributions to human survey data across racial groups (White, Black, Asian, Hispanic, Other).
Hypothesis testing comparing LLM-simulated response distributions to human survey data across age cohorts (18-29, 30-49, 50-64, 65+).
Hypothesis testing comparing LLM-simulated response distributions to human survey data across income levels and educational attainment.
Hypothesis testing comparing LLM-simulated response distributions to human survey data across sex (Male, Female).
Hypothesis testing comparing LLM-simulated response distributions to human survey data across political ideologies (Conservative, Liberal) and parties (Republican, Democrat).
Hypothesis testing comparing LLM-simulated response distributions to human survey data across religious affiliations and attendance frequencies.
Hypothesis testing comparing LLM-simulated response distributions to human survey data across marital statuses (Married, Widowed, Divorced, etc.).
Hypothesis testing comparing LLM-simulated response distributions to human survey data across U.S. census regions (Northeast, Midwest, South, West).
